key_idea: Just simulate the described greedy: sort all n*m (distance, judge, repository) triples and sweep, taking a pair whenever both endpoints are still free.
sketch: For tar and feathers separately, generate all up to 1e6 judge-site pairs, keyed by integer squared distance, then judge index, then site index (packed into one 64-bit key so ties break exactly as the statement demands). Sort and scan, matching a pair when neither side is used, adding sqrt of the squared distance, stopping after n matches. O(nm log(nm)) per phase, about 2e6 keys total. Pitfalls: compare squared integer distances rather than doubles so tie-breaking is exact, and the tie order is judge first then repository.
